heroText: Monrovia is Liberia's capital, named for US President James Monroe and set on a peninsula between the Atlantic and the Mesurado River. First-time visitors should learn the country's founding story at the National Museum of Liberia, walk historic Providence Island where freed settlers first landed, and photograph the abandoned Ducor Palace Hotel on its clifftop. Roberts International Airport connects the city to the rest of West Africa.

areas.name: Mamba Point
areas.text: Mamba Point is Monrovia's embassy and hotel district on the coast, close to government buildings and popular with business travelers.

areas.name: Sinkor
areas.text: Sinkor stretches along the beachfront with hotels, restaurants and residential streets, a comfortable base for longer stays.

areas.name: Central Monrovia
areas.text: Central Monrovia around Broad Street holds the main shops, banks and the National Museum, useful for a first, walkable stay.

airports.name: Roberts International Airport (ROB)
airports.text: Roberts International Airport lies about 60km southeast of central Monrovia, so confirm a pre-arranged transfer given the distance and limited late-night options.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Roberts International Airport (ROB) and central Monrovia before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in Mamba Point for embassies and coastal hotels, or Sinkor for beachfront restaurants and a relaxed longer stay. Central Monrovia suits a first visit wanting easy walking access to Broad Street's shops and the National Museum.
hotelIntro: Monrovia hotel choice depends on purpose: Mamba Point suits business and diplomatic travelers, Sinkor suits longer beachfront stays with restaurants, and Central Monrovia keeps you closest to Broad Street's shops and museums.
rentalCars: A rental car with a driver is the practical option for the long transfer from Roberts International Airport and any trips beyond the city; self-drive is uncommon for visitors.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose the Monrovia base by repeat journeys: sights, evening food, station access and the airport transfer should all still work.

travelTips.title: Airport transfer
travelTips.text: Arrange a hotel transfer in advance for the roughly 60km drive from Roberts International Airport, which can take over an hour.

travelTips.title: Cash
travelTips.text: Carry both US dollars and Liberian dollars in small denominations, since both currencies circulate for everyday purchases.

travelTips.title: Rainy season
travelTips.text: Plan around the heavy rainy season from May to October, when flooding can slow roads and shorten sightseeing time.

nearbyIdeas.label: Beach
nearbyIdeas.text: Robertsport, a few hours west, is West Africa's best-known surf town, with long point breaks and a laid-back beach village feel.

nearbyIdeas.text: Kakata, an hour inland, offers cooler forested scenery and a look at rural Liberian life away from the capital.

history.label: Origins
history.text: President James Monroe, a prominent supporter of the colonization of Liberia and the American Colonization Society (ACS).

The agreement, which covered a relatively small coastal area and was valued at approximately $300 in trade goods, has been the subject of historical debate, with modern scholarship revisiting earlier claims about the circumstances.
The French cartographer and slave trader Chevalier des Marchais visited Ducor and the Cape in 1723, conducted business there and later published a map of the area.
Before 1816, the area around Cape Mesurado and the mouth of the Mesurado River was called Ducor.
He likewise signed into law the Anti-Slave Trading Act of 1819, which funded the ACS's mission to create such a colony in West Africa.
Prior to the establishment of the settlement, representatives of the American Colonization Society negotiated the purchase of land at Cape Mesurado in December 1821 from local leaders.
On 7 January 1822, a ship took these settlers to Dazoe Island (now called Providence Island) at the mouth of the Mesurado River.
In 1824, the city was renamed Monrovia after James Monroe, president of the United States at the time.

history.label: Growth
history.text: Along with Washington, D.C., it is one of two world capitals to be named after an American president.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: It had long been established as a crossroads and a place of trade inhabited by fishing, trading and farming communities of various ethnicities, including the Dey, Kru, Bassa, Gola, and Vai.
